name: Vermaland La Osa Data Center Park
transmission_utility: Arizona Public Service (APS) / Salt River Project (SRP)
additional_info: 3,300-acre site in Pinal County, federally designated Qualified Opportunity Zone in Phoenix-Tucson corridor. Up to 3 GW capacity; would rival Northern Virginia Data Center Alley. source: Commercial Property Executive, August 1, 2025: https://www.commercialsearch.com/news/33b-data-center-park-eyed-in-arizona/ | Blackridge Research AZ, 2026: https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/latest-list-upcoming-data-centers-in-arizona-az-united-states-us
address: Near Eloy, Pinal County, AZ (south of Phoenix, north of Tucson)

name: Aligned Data Centers Glendale Campus PHX-13
additional_info: 100-acre Glendale campus; PHX-13 is first of 4 planned facilities on campus. 72 MW capacity. Broke ground April 15, 2025. Aligned Delta³ air cooling arrays + closed-loop water recycling. New 230 kV APS transmission line to support campus.
source: Blackridge Research AZ, 2026: https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/latest-list-upcoming-data-centers-in-arizona-az-united-states-us | AZ Tech Council: https://www.aztechcouncil.org/8-metro-phoenix-data-center-developments-to-watch/

name: EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure Mesa Campus Expansion
additional_info: Expansion of existing Mesa campus (206 MW operational). Added 44-acre parcel (May 2025) bringing campus to 43.87 total acres. Full buildout 450 MW, 3.1M+ sqft. Expansion of 250 MW+ under construction for 2025/2026 delivery. Previously EdgeCore announced May 21, 2025. SRP is utility provider.
source: Commercial Property Executive, August 2025: https://www.commercialsearch.com/news/33b-data-center-park-eyed-in-arizona/ | Blackridge Research AZ, 2026: https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/latest-list-upcoming-data-centers-in-arizona-az-united-states-us
address: Elliot Road Technology Corridor, Mesa, AZ

name: NTT Data Mesa Campus 2 (Pecos/Crismon)
additional_info: 173 acres acquired March 2025, a few miles south of NTT's existing Elliot Road campus. First building (36 MW) targeted to open November 2028. Part of NTT $10B global expansion plan. Seven buildings planned. Combined capacity across both Mesa campuses: under 600 MW.
address: Northeast corner of Pecos and Crismon Roads, Mesa, AZ

name: Takanock Phoenix Data Center Campus
additional_info: Two data center buildings proposed near Phoenix. Building 1 targeted online Q1 2028; Building 2 Q1 2030. Maricopa County Development Permit application and Certificate of Environmental Compatibility application submitted. 1,000 construction jobs + 200 permanent roles. Takanock: 4 active US sites, 2.8 GW IT capacity, 5.3 GW generation capacity; raised $500M June 2025. Active in Northern Virginia. EPCOR for water/sewer.

name: Tract Buckeye Technology Park
additional_info: Up to 20 million sqft data center space across 40 individual data centers. Full buildout expected over 15 years. Currently in planning stage. MW capacity not disclosed.

name: Amazon Web Services Tucson Data Center (rejected)
additional_info: Tucson City Council unanimously rejected proposed Amazon Web Services data center in August 2025. Community opposition over water use, electricity demand, and proximity to residential areas. Cited in Nevada Current January 2026 as example of Southwest community pushback.

name: Page Arizona Data Center (referendum)
additional_info: Page residents filed a referendum in December 2025 to stop a proposed data center on the banks of the Colorado River. Concerns about water use from an already stressed river system serving multiple southwestern states.

name: Vantage Data Centers Storey County Campus (NV1)
additional_info: 137 acres at Tahoe Reno Industrial Center (TRIC). 1.1M sqft, 4 four-story buildings. First building ready Q2 2026. Power ramp from NV Energy through 2029. If all power secured, would lease all 224 MW immediately. $3B total investment. 5-story excavation required due to hilly terrain.
address: Corner of Electric Avenue and USA Parkway, Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, NV

name: EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure TRIC Campus (Nevada)
additional_info: 900,000 sqft data center at TRIC. Air-cooled closed-loop chiller (no water evaporation). Under construction as of mid-2025. MW capacity not publicly disclosed. Part of Google, Tract, Switch, EdgeCore, Novva, Vantage, PowerHouse TRIC cluster.
address: Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, NV

name: Lyon County 14-Building Data Center Complex
additional_info: 14-building complex on 500+ acres of agricultural land rezoned by Lyon County Planning Commission (unanimous vote). 1,000 MW power requirement — enough electricity for ~500,000 homes. Water concerns: Mason Valley is one of Nevada's most overtapped groundwater basins where farmers already face cuts due to decades-long groundwater decline. Developer identity not publicly disclosed.
address: Mason Valley, approximately 10 miles north of Yerington, Lyon County, NV

name: Novva Tahoe Reno Data Center
additional_info: 300,000 sqft, 20-acre campus. Novva's 4th data center location. Launched January 2026. Supports 250 kW to 30 MW deployments. Air-cooled. New capacity available in 2026. Novva pipeline: 4 additional locations in development including San Francisco, Mesa AZ, North Las Vegas 2, Utah 2 — totaling 1 GW+.
address: 3399 Peru Drive, McCarran, NV 89437 (Tahoe Reno Industrial Center)

name: Project Jupiter (Oracle / OpenAI / BorderPlex Digital)
additional_info: Massive AI data center campus in Santa Teresa, southeastern New Mexico near US-Mexico border. Doña Ana County approved tax incentives. Part of Stargate initiative. Power: April 27, 2026 Oracle and BorderPlex announced Bloom Energy fuel cells replacing gas turbines + diesel generators — dramatic water use reduction, better air quality. NM State Land Commissioner rejected application for gas pipeline March 31, 2026. Federal regulatory staff protested proposed pipeline April 17, 2026. Gallup City Council deferred related wastewater agreement April 29, 2026. Total investment $165B if fully built out.
source: Source New Mexico, April 27, 2026: https://sourcenm.com/2026/04/27/nm-project-jupiter-data-center-developers-announce-new-plans-for-generating-power/ | Data Center Knowledge, May 2026: https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-construction/new-data-center-developments-may-2026
address: Santa Teresa, Doña Ana County, NM

name: New Era Energy & Digital Lea County AI Campus
additional_info: Hyperscale AI campus in Lea County, NM (Permian Basin oil/gas epicenter). Announced November 2025. Planned own nuclear + gas power plants with combined ~7 GW generation capacity. Campus will be "so big" it needs its own power generation. MW capacity of data center IT load not separately disclosed from generation capacity.
source: High Country News / Maven's Notebook, November 27, 2025: https://mavensnotebook.com/2025/11/25/high-country-news-the-big-data-center-buildup/

name: Project Jade / Switchgrass Industrial Park (Crusoe Energy)
additional_info: Laramie County unanimously approved January 5, 2026. AI data center campus (Crusoe Energy) + BFC Power/Cheyenne Power Hub (Tallgrass Energy, $7B energy infrastructure). Phase 1: 2.7 GW natural gas generation. Full buildout target: 10 GW. Energy infrastructure alone = $7B. Total CapEx likely >$50B. "Bring your own power" self-sufficient model. Bloom Energy fuel cells also planned. Plans to add additional generation for further scaling. Local concerns: water contamination risk, countryside views.
source: Power Magazine, January 12, 2026: https://www.powermag.com/wyoming-approves-data-center-campus-that-includes-2-7-gw-of-new-natural-gas-fired-generation/ | Data Center Knowledge May 2026: https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-construction/new-data-center-developments-may-2026
address: Switchgrass Industrial Park, Laramie County, WY (near Cheyenne)
transmission_upgrades.description: "Bring your own power" model — designed to be self-sufficient

name: Prometheus Hyperscale Evanston Data Center
additional_info: 1,200 MW natural gas-powered hyperscale data center in Evanston, WY. Marketed as "sustainable" with cold Northern Rockies climate for cooling, water recycling, efficient servers, server heat reuse for greenhouses and aquaculture (shrimp farming). Initial power: natural gas, carbon offset by paying for carbon capture at biofuel plants in Nebraska. Future: nuclear micro-reactors planned. Not yet operational. Talked about since 2024.
source: High Country News / Maven's Notebook, November 27, 2025: https://mavensnotebook.com/2025/11/25/high-country-news-the-big-data-center-buildup/

name: Microsoft Cheyenne Data Center Expansion (Phase 2)
additional_info: Microsoft announced intent to purchase ~3,200 acres in Cheyenne April 14, 2026. Two parcels: ~200 acres in Bison Business Park on Wapiti Trail, and ~3,000 acres in SE Cheyenne adjacent to Bison Business Park. Builds on existing Cheyenne facilities since 2012. Microsoft was #1 taxpayer in Cheyenne 2025, $11M+ to Laramie County tax base. Direct evaporative cooling used <10% of year; latest designs eliminate ongoing water need. Replenishment commitments: 566M gallons in Colorado + Mississippi-Missouri basins. Community investment: $4.7M to local organizations since 2018.
address: Phase 2A: Bison Business Park, Wapiti Trail east of S Greeley Hwy (~200 acres); Phase 2B: SE Cheyenne (~3,000 acres)

name: Stratos Delta AI Data Center Campus (Kevin O'Leary / O'Shares)
additional_info: MIDA (Military Installation Development Authority) approved. 40,000 acres (~161 km²), Juab/Millard County. 9 GW full buildout — more than double Utah's entire current grid usage. Powered off-grid via connection to Ruby Pipeline; will "not take one electron" from existing grid; may eventually feed surplus back to grid. Approved amid controversy: would produce more emissions than entire state of Utah. Multiple data center companies also eyeing Delta UT near Intermountain Power Project (coal-to-gas/hydrogen conversion).
source: Tom's Hardware, May 2026: https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/kevin-o-learys-9-gw-utah-data-center-campus-approved | High Country News / Maven's Notebook: https://mavensnotebook.com/2025/11/25/high-country-news-the-big-data-center-buildup/
address: Delta, Millard County, UT (near Intermountain Power Project)

name: Imperial County Hyperscale AI Data Center (Rucci)
developer: Sebastian Rucci (developer, name not yet entity)
additional_info: Nearly 1M sqft computing warehouse. $10B investment. Serving one major tech company (unnamed). Electricity demand could equal all of Imperial County's 2024 consumption. 750,000 gallons water/day. City of Imperial filed lawsuit Dec 2025 alleging inadequate environmental review. Developer seeking to bypass CEQA. Originally proposed within city limits; relocated to county land after initial opposition. Residents organizing November 2026 ballot initiative: "Imperial County Data Center Prohibition Act." El Centro issued conditional water service letter October 2025 (not a final agreement). Imperial has not committed to water agreement. Developer's business history in Ohio includes criminal investigations.
address: Aten Road and Clark Road, Imperial County, CA (adjacent to city of Imperial)

name: Goodman Group San Jose Data Center Campus
additional_info: 45.8-acre infill property acquired October 28, 2025 from LBA Realty affiliate for $200M. Two-building campus, 414,000 sqft. Currently occupied by Lumileds (lighting manufacturer) until October 2026; renamed "Goodman Innovation Centre San Jose." Two existing R&D buildings (500,350 sqft) available for lease Oct 2026. Data center operational by 2028.
address: 350 & 370 West Trimble Road, Santa Clara County (San Jose), CA

name: DataBank Goodman Group Vernon Joint Venture
additional_info: Joint venture between DataBank and Goodman Group. 32 MW facility targeting one of the most supply-constrained data center markets in the US. Vernon announced it will tap remaining available power for additional capacity. Development to begin 2026 per JLL report.
source: Data Center Knowledge, May 2026: https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-construction/new-data-center-developments-may-2026 | GlobeSt, February 20, 2026: https://www.globest.com/amp/2026/02/20/investors-eye-data-center-construction-in-california-as-availability-remains-scarce/
address: Vernon, CA (5.2-sq-mile industrial city southeast of downtown LA)

name: Digital Realty Los Angeles (near One Wilshire)
transmission_utility: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
additional_info: 13-story facility near One Wilshire. 5 acres, 485,892 sqft. Land purchased November 6, 2025 for $49M from LLC tied to 4D Development & Investments (founder David Pourbaba) via Pacific Santa Fe Industrial LLC. Existing 253,200 sqft industrial building (1925) on site. Part of Digital Realty LA expansion in supply-constrained market.
address: Near One Wilshire, Los Angeles, CA (5-acre parcel, 1925 industrial building)

name: Oakley Data Center Moratorium
additional_info: Oakley City Council voted unanimously to impose 45-day moratorium blocking city from accepting, processing, or approving any land use applications tied to data centers. First Bay Area city to take such action (May 2026). Triggered by concerns about energy demand, water use, and community impacts from AI-era data centers.

name: Hansel Valley Data Center
additional_info: Approved plan for a 40,000-acre data center in Hansel Valley, estimated to cost over $1 billion.

name: Google Nevada Data Center Expansion
additional_info: Google plans to expand its data center operations in Nevada by securing up to 150 MW of geothermal energy through a PPA with NV Energy.
